entries.clue: Bug found in chicken served by swimmer (9)

indicatorNotes.served by: a dish served by something has it placed alongside, so ROACH comes next

blocks.note: a cock is a male chicken
a roach is a freshwater fish

annotation.surface: A diner discovers an insect in their chicken, which came with a side of fish.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Swimmer' in crosswords is often a fish rather than a person; here it is the roach, a common European freshwater fish.
annotation.definitionFit: A cockroach is an insect, and 'bug' is everyday English for any insect.

entries.clue: Red cumin? Most unusual! (9)

indicatorNotes.unusual: the letters are put into an unusual order

annotation.surface: Someone exclaims that a batch of cumin has come out red, which is very odd.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark and exclamation split the fodder across two sentences, hiding that 'Most' belongs with 'cumin'. 'Red' as a noun is a standard label for a communist.
annotation.definitionFit: A standing nickname: the red flag is the banner of the left, so 'Red' labels its followers.

entries.clue: Shell of blue; skin of Cheetah (5)

indicatorNotes.skin of: the skin is the outside, so only the first and last letters of Cheetah are kept

blocks.note: blue is the colour of the Conservatives, abbreviated CON

annotation.surface: A catalogue of animal colourings: a blue shell next to a cheetah's pelt.
annotation.walkthrough: In British politics the Conservative party's colour is blue, so 'blue' can clue CON (and TORY).
annotation.definitionFit: A conch is a large spiral seashell.

entries.clue: English performer in band making a comeback (9)

indicatorNotes.in: E and TURN sit inside RING

blocks.note: a ring is a band, as on a finger
a turn is a variety performer or act

annotation.surface: An English musician rejoins their old group for a reunion tour.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Band' pushes towards a music group, but it is the ring. A 'turn' is an old music-hall word for a performer's act, and by extension the performer.
annotation.definitionFit: Returning is coming back, which is what making a comeback means.

entries.clue: Walking slowly being better? Good to be discharged! (7)

indicatorNotes.to be discharged: the G is sent away from the word

blocks.note: a better is one who bets, so being a better is gambling

annotation.surface: A patient on a slow walk asks whether they are improving and hopes to be sent home.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Better' reads as 'improved', which suits a hospital picture; it is one who bets.
annotation.definitionFit: To amble is to walk at a slow, easy pace.

entries.clue: Heroin plus drink? Show me who'd like some of this? (5,2)

annotation.definition: Show me who'd like some of this?
annotation.surface: A dealer offers heroin and a drink to a crowd and asks who's interested.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is a whole question, the sort a teacher asks a class before a show of hands.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Hands up' is the call that asks people to show who wants something.

entries.clue: Swift ends of legs? Littler's bound to be involved! (5)

indicatorNotes.bound: a bound is a boundary or edge, so Littler's bound is its first letter
indicatorNotes.to be involved: to involve is to wrap up or enfold, so FEET wraps itself around the L

blocks.note: feet are at the ends of legs

annotation.surface: Speculation about Luke Littler, the teenage darts champion, and how quick on his feet he is.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bound' looks like a leap, which suits 'Swift' and 'legs'; here it is the boundary of the word. Luke Littler is the teenage darts world champion.
annotation.definitionFit: Fleet is an adjective meaning fast, as in 'fleet of foot'.

entries.clue: A trawler at front entering river terminal (5)

indicatorNotes.at front: only the front letter of trawler is used
indicatorNotes.entering: A and T go into the river's name

blocks.note: the Fal is a river in Cornwall

annotation.surface: A fishing boat noses into a river port's terminal.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Terminal' reads as a harbour building, which fits the trawler; it is the adjective for an illness that kills. The Fal is a river in Cornwall: F(A T)AL.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonyms in the medical sense: an illness that will end in death.

entries.clue: Old auditor perhaps on call in Treasury department (9)

indicatorNotes.on call: a call is a spoken word, so CHECKER is heard rather than spelt

blocks.note: an auditor is one example of a checker

annotation.surface: A retired auditor is on standby for work in a government finance office.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' marks auditor as one example of a checker. 'On call' reads as being available for work; it is the homophone signal.
annotation.definitionFit: The Exchequer is the British government department in charge of public money, the Treasury.

entries.clue: Surprise gift: upside-down pastry laced with MDMA (5)

indicatorNotes.upside-down: in a down entry, turning a word upside down reads it bottom to top
indicatorNotes.laced with: E is threaded into the pastry

blocks.note: a tart is a pastry, turned over
MDMA is the drug ecstasy, E

annotation.surface: A spiked upside-down tart handed over as a gift.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Upside-down' sounds like a baking style (pineapple upside-down cake), but it turns TART over in this down clue. TR(E)AT.
annotation.definitionFit: A treat is an unexpected pleasure given to someone.

entries.clue: Canadian chap in boat in a state of distress (9)

indicatorNotes.in a state of distress: the letters of IN BOAT are thrown into disorder

annotation.surface: A Canadian man is adrift in a boat and in trouble.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a container word placing a man inside a boat; it is part of the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: A Manitoban comes from Manitoba, a Canadian province.

entries.clue: Attachés covering up something right under Poirot's nose? (5)

indicatorNotes.covering up: the word Attachés conceals the answer inside it

annotation.surface: Diplomatic staff are hiding something that the detective Poirot has missed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Right under his nose' is the idiom for something missed; literally, it is Poirot's famous moustache. Tache is British slang for moustache.
annotation.definitionFit: Poirot, Agatha Christie's detective, has a famous moustache, which sits right under his nose.

entries.clue: It's a job being American in this place mostly (5)

indicatorNotes.mostly: most of the word is kept, dropping its last letter

annotation.surface: Someone notes that being American is practically a job around here.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition hides at the front as a throwaway phrase; an usher is a job in a theatre or church.
annotation.definitionFit: Ushering is a job: showing people to their seats.

entries.clue: Penniless Poles involved in violent rioting (9)

indicatorNotes.involved in: N and S are taken into the mix
indicatorNotes.rioting: the letters of VIOLENT run riot

blocks.note: the north and south poles, N and S

annotation.surface: Broke Polish workers take part in a violent riot.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Poles' reads as Polish people; in crosswords it is usually N and S, the magnetic poles.
annotation.definitionFit: Insolvent means unable to pay debts, so without money.

entries.clue: Impatient moaning bishop needs excommunicating! (7)

indicatorNotes.needs excommunicating: the bishop is thrown out of the word

blocks.note: B = bishop in chess notation, removed

annotation.surface: A complaining, restless bishop ought to be thrown out of the church.
annotation.walkthrough: Excommunication suits the churchly surface, but here it simply expels the letter B.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: someone itching to go is restless and eager, like a person who cannot stop scratching.

entries.clue: Part of a SEAT a chick smashed up with bar (9)

indicatorNotes.smashed up: the letters are broken and put back in a new order

annotation.surface: A car seat (SEAT is a Spanish car brand) gets wrecked in a bar brawl.
annotation.walkthrough: The capitals on SEAT point at the Spanish car maker, but capitals can always be ignored: this is just a seat.
annotation.definitionFit: The chairback is the upright part of a chair, a kind of seat.

entries.clue: A flipping curt bruiser could cause trouble (7)

indicatorNotes.flipping: to flip something is to turn it over, so BRUT is read backwards
indicatorNotes.curt: curt means cut short, so BRUTE loses its last letter

blocks.note: per = a, as in ten pounds a head
a bruiser is a BRUTE, cut short to BRUT and flipped

annotation.surface: A rude thug is likely to start a fight.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' reads as a mild British swear word; 'curt' reads as rude. Both are instructions. PER for 'a' is a crossword staple.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean to unsettle someone and make them anxious.

entries.clue: Those wading by shore send shark into a frenzy (9)

indicatorNotes.into a frenzy: the letters are whipped into a frenzy, like feeding sharks

annotation.surface: Paddlers near the beach set off a shark feeding frenzy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Those wading' suggests people paddling; redshanks are wading birds of the shoreline.
annotation.definitionFit: The redshank is a red-legged wading bird of coasts and marshes.

entries.clue: IT meeting arranged by phone? (5,4)

blocks.note: surface: a session with the computer people; meant: a meeting for IT, meaning sex
the call that sets it up; the question mark flags the double reading

annotation.surface: An IT department schedules a meeting over the phone.
annotation.walkthrough: 'IT' looks like information technology; its old sense is sex (as in 'the It girl'). A booty call is a call made to arrange sex.
annotation.definitionFit: A booty call is a phone call or message arranging a casual sexual meeting.

entries.clue: Time pale German with my boss picked a G-string? (7)

blocks.note: the setter's boss is the editor, ED

annotation.surface: A pale German and the speaker's boss choose some skimpy underwear.
annotation.walkthrough: A G-string reads as underwear; on a guitar or violin it is the string tuned to G, and picking it twangs it.
annotation.definitionFit: Plucking an instrument string makes it twang, so a picked G-string was twanged.

entries.clue: Torpid bouncer? One ball not delivered by Trueman primarily! (7)

indicatorNotes.not delivered: one O is kept back, as a ball never bowled
indicatorNotes.primarily: only the first letter of Trueman is used

blocks.note: a bouncer is a nightclub doorman
a ball is round like O; one O is removed

annotation.surface: Cricket talk: Fred Trueman, the England fast bowler, sluggishly failing to bowl a bouncer.
annotation.walkthrough: In cricket a bouncer is a short ball that rears up; here it is the doorman. Fred Trueman was a famous England fast bowler, which sells the cricket picture.
annotation.definitionFit: Dormant and torpid both mean inactive or sluggish.

entries.clue: Sustain less than good offspring (at first) (7)

indicatorNotes.at first: only the first letter of offspring is taken

annotation.surface: A parent must put up with children who are less than good.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Less than good' reads as one phrase about behaviour; it splits into UNDER and G.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym when talking of injuries or losses: both mean to experience and bear them.

entries.clue: A French composer and soprano’s releases (7)

blocks.note: S = soprano, as in SATB choir parts

annotation.surface: A French composer and a soprano issue new recordings.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Releases' reads as a record label's new albums; it is the verb for setting free. The 's is a contraction of 'is' joining the two halves.
annotation.definitionFit: To uncage an animal is to release it.

entries.clue: Old and new Cartier rings one put on gangsta (9)

indicatorNotes.new: CARTIER is made new by rearranging
indicatorNotes.put on: the whole is placed after G

blocks.note: G is slang for a gangsta

annotation.surface: A gangsta shows off Cartier rings, some vintage, some new.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rings' looks like jewellery, fitting Cartier; it is a container verb. 'G' as a greeting for a gangsta ('what up, G') is slang.
annotation.definitionFit: Geriatric means relating to old people, and loosely just old.

entries.clue: Head to Goa with relative to get wasted (5)

indicatorNotes.Head to: the head of Goa is its first letter

annotation.surface: Heading to Goa, the Indian party beach, with an aunt to get drunk.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Head to Goa' reads as a travel plan and 'wasted' as drunk; the head is G, and wasted means thin and worn.
annotation.definitionFit: Gaunt means thin and haggard, as a wasted body is.

entries.clue: Old Afghan leader always after a maiden (5)

indicatorNotes.after: after means following in order, so EER is written following A and M

blocks.note: M = maiden, a cricket over with no runs

annotation.surface: An old Afghan ruler forever chasing after a young woman.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Maiden' reads as a young woman; in cricket scoring it is a maiden over, M. The apostrophe of e'er is dropped.
annotation.definitionFit: An ameer (emir) was the title of the rulers of Afghanistan.

entries.clue: Enduring author? (5)

blocks.note: an adjective: tough, able to survive hard conditions
a writer's surname: the Victorian novelist of Wessex

annotation.walkthrough: Two words, two meanings: an adjective and a surname. The question mark flags that 'author' is one example.
annotation.definitionFit: Hardy things endure hardship, and Thomas Hardy wrote Tess of the d'Urbervilles.

entries.clue: Increase level of sound (5)

indicatorNotes.of sound: the answer is what 'level' sounds like as another word

blocks.note: to raze a building is to level it

annotation.surface: Turn the volume up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Increase level of sound' reads as 'turn it up'; 'level' is the verb raze, which sounds like raise.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: pushing a price, a wage or a volume upward.

entries.clue: Employment you and me found by centre of Hagen (5)

indicatorNotes.centre of: only the middle letters of Hagen are taken

annotation.surface: Two people find jobs in the middle of the German town of Hagen.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Employment' reads as jobs, but it means use, as in the employment of a tool.
annotation.definitionFit: Employment in its older sense of putting something to use, not of having a job.

entries.clue: Spy screening king visiting a foreign country (9)

indicatorNotes.screening: AGENT screens R by holding it inside
indicatorNotes.visiting: a visitor is somewhere, so visiting 'a' puts the reader IN A

blocks.note: a secret agent is a spy
R = rex, king, placed inside: A(R)GENT
visiting means being in, so IN A

annotation.surface: A spy guarding a king on a state visit abroad.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Screening' reads as vetting or protecting; it is hiding R inside AGENT. The 'a' is wordplay, so the definition is only 'foreign country'.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: any country abroad would do, and this South American one fits the letters.

entries.clue: Batman villain making judge tense is a drug-taker (5)

indicatorNotes.making: the judge is made into tense: J becomes T

annotation.surface: Batman's villain turns out to be using drugs, which makes the judge anxious.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tense' reads as nervous; in grammar a tense is abbreviated T.
annotation.definitionFit: A toker is one who takes tokes, puffs on a cannabis joint.

entries.clue: Animal skulls he set out on centre of altar (4,5)

indicatorNotes.set out: the letters are laid out anew
indicatorNotes.centre of: only the middle letter of altar is used

annotation.surface: A sinister rite: someone lays out animal skulls on an altar.
annotation.walkthrough: The ritual picture pulls 'Animal' into the scene as the skulls' owner; it is the definition. A tusk shell is a sea mollusc with a tusk-shaped shell.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the creature is a sea mollusc, named for its tapering shell.
